ORBIT.goal: recover multiplicative order from residue collisions

RELATION.goal: recover congruence-of-squares/factor receipts independently of multiplicative-order recovery
RELATION.implementation_scope: Fermat-style scout in v0; successor may use stronger relation collection only under new preregistration

fusion.SPIDER: cross-core graph may relate exact residue collisions, order divisibility, congruence-of-squares and factor receipts
fusion.KEYMASTER: routes certified hints between cores but may not declare correctness
fusion.PIPPI: keeps separate compute, latency, memory, negative-result and provenance ledgers
fusion.MAD_LAB: constructs worst-case semiprimes for both cores jointly

laws: two cores do not imply a better complexity class
parallel work is summed for total compute
only exact certificates cross the authority boundary
a finite scale fit is not an asymptotic proof
failure of either or both cores is preserved
polynomial-time factoring requires a formal poly(log N) worst-case bound for all valid inputs
polynomial_factoring_terminal_gate: correctness proved for all composite inputs in scope
worst-case total bit complexity proved polynomial in n=ceil(log2 N)
all intermediate memory/representations polynomial in n
proof independent of finite benchmarks, model confidence, or parallel-latency arguments
note: Even a proof of polynomial-time integer factoring would not by itself establish P=NP.
